# Reverberation Modeling Workshop Problem XI waveguide, 1 kHz: transmission loss from a
# wavenumber-integration solution.
# 
# Problem: Problem XI of the Reverberation Modeling Workshop (University of Texas at Austin,
# November 2006), as Ainslie, Principles of Sonar Performance Modelling (2010), Sect. 9.4.1.2,
# Table 9.4 and Fig. 9.26 give it (RMW11): water 100 m deep, sound speed 1500 m/s, source 30 m,
# receiver 50 m, over a fine-sand half-space of 1700 m/s, density ratio 2 and 0.5 dB per
# wavelength. The workshop frequencies are 250 Hz, 1 kHz and 3.5 kHz (Etter, Underwater Acoustic
# Modeling and Simulation, Sect. 12.2). The workshop problem asks for reverberation in water with
# a volume attenuation (0.2397 dB/km at 3.5 kHz in Ainslie's Fig. 9.26); this table is the
# transmission loss of its environment with lossless water.
# 
# Solution: the Acoustics Toolbox's SCOOTER (wavenumber integration, exact for this
# range-independent problem up to discretisation) run through uacpy on
# Environment(water_density=1.0) with a density-2.0 half-space, as Scooter(c_high=1e9), i.e.
# integrating from k = 0, at its other defaults (c_low 0.9 x 1500 m/s = 1350 m/s, RMax 2 x 10 km,
# 59259 wavenumbers). Discretisation over 0.1-10 km: rmax_factor=4 moves it 0.0068 dB median,
# 0.0229 dB 90th percentile; c_low 1200 m/s 0.0051 / 0.0201 dB. Cross-checked against OASES OAST
# run through uacpy at its defaults: 0.0277 dB median and 0.1200 dB
# 90th-percentile |dTL| over 0.1-10 km.
# 
# TL is dB re 1 m.
# 
# range_km  TL_50m_dB
